record.title: A paper introduces a five-platform benchmark for hybrid computer-use agents and reports a large gap between aggregate scores and full behavioral tests
record.summary: The authors introduce RecreationWorld, a framework for training and evaluating agents that alternate between exploring a running application through its interface, implementing a recreation in code, and executing it for feedback across Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Android and Web. Their held-out RecreationBench has 250 tasks and reference-grounded hidden tests. In the authors’ evaluation of ten models, GPT-6 Astra scored 58.06% overall, but only 2.8% of tasks had a full programmatic pass; the paper reports that interface structure was reproduced more reliably than interactions and computed outputs. These are author-reported results from a new benchmark, not an independent capability comparison or a measure of general computer-use ability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors present a framework that combines GUI exploration, coding and execution/visual verification in reproducible Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Android and Web environments.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the authors’ 250-task RecreationBench, they report GPT-6 Astra at 58.06% overall, ahead of Claude Opus 5 at 44.16%; only 2.8% of tasks had full programmatic passes for GPT-6 Astra.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that agents reproduce static interface structure more reliably than interactions and computed outputs on their benchmark.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent team has rerun RecreationBench or checked whether its hidden tests and scores generalize to other computer-use tasks.
Transfer beyond reference-recreation tasks, the five supported platforms and the paper’s model/harness configurations is not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If useful beyond the authors’ benchmark, a five-platform environment joining GUI operation, coding and execution-grounded verification could change how long-horizon computer-use agents are trained and evaluated. Its significance is major for this subfield, while benchmark representativeness and reported model results remain unreplicated.
limitations: Results are reported by the paper authors and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
RecreationBench comprises 250 reference-recreation tasks; its representativeness of real computer-use work and transfer to other task formulations remain uncertain.
The overall score is not equivalent to full task correctness; 2.8% full programmatic pass coverage for GPT-6 Astra is the paper’s reported value under its scoring protocol.
The benchmark compares the listed frontier models under paper-specific inference configurations; it does not establish general ranking across workloads, prompts, models or harnesses.
The reported association between broader exploration and stronger scores is descriptive and does not establish that exploration caused the performance difference.

Their held-out RecreationBench has 250 tasks and reference-grounded hidden tests. In the authors’ evaluation of ten models, GPT-6 Astra scored 58.06% overall, but only 2.8% of tasks had a full programmatic pass; the paper reports that interface structure was reproduced more reliably than interactions and computed outputs. technical.claimed_result: Authors report GPT-6 Astra achieved 58.06% aggregate score (Claude Opus 5 44.16%) and that GPT-6 Astra obtained full programmatic passes on tasks totaling 2.8% coverage. They report static structure was reproduced more reliably than interactions and computed outputs.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected v2 paper contains the framework description, benchmark protocol and reported results. The release artifacts and model evaluations were not independently rerun here.
technical.mechanism: Agents alternate GUI exploration, code implementation and execution/visual verification while reproducing an application from a running reference. Reference behavior supports hidden programmatic and visual assertions; the framework also uses generated trajectories for training.
technical.regime: Five-platform framework across Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Android and Web; 250 held-out benchmark tasks; ten frontier models evaluated using the paper’s specified direct-MCP configurations.
technical.reproducibility: The paper points to benchmark and environment releases; this activation inspected the paper but did not download/run the artifacts or independently verify their completeness.
technical.strongest_baseline: The reported model comparison includes ten frontier systems; GPT-6 Astra is compared with Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol under the paper’s benchmark configurations. This is not an independently matched evaluation across all inference stacks.

brief.title: A paper introduces a five-platform benchmark for hybrid computer-use agents and reports a large gap between aggregate scores and full behavioral tests
brief.why_it_matters: Computer-use agents often need to combine interface exploration with code changes and then verify the running result. RecreationWorld offers a way to train that loop and score behavior against an executable reference. Its reported results also show why an aggregate score can overstate full behavioral fidelity: the leading model’s score was 58.06%, while full programmatic passes covered 2.8% of tasks in this benchmark. Independent replication and transfer beyond the authors’ task set remain open.
